All six files pass `node --check`. Before I call this done, I want to confirm that every `@/lib/reports/*` import resolves to a file I created, and that the only remaining unresolved imports are the external `@/app/api/utils/*` modules the original also depended on.

The refactor is in place and every file passes a syntax check. I could not run the handler end to end, because the `@/app/api/utils/*` modules it depends on are not in this workspace.

## Result

`src/app/route.js` is now a 50-line handler. It still exports only `GET`, the same as before, and keeps the same flow: `requireAccess`, URL parsing, the 400 check, then the queries in the original order.

Logic moved into `src/lib/reports/`:

- **`filters.js`**: parses query params and builds parameterised WHERE clauses (`createWhere`, `addWhere`, `addDateRange`).
- **`summaries.js`**: policy, quote and claims summaries, plus `computeConversionRate`.
- **`assessors.js`**: assessor performance, which ignores date filters.
- **`trends.js`**: monthly policy and claim trends, with the 6-month default when no `date_from` is given.
- **`breakdown.js`**: quotes by cover type.

## Behaviour

- Placeholder numbering and parameter order match the original for every query. I checked each branch against the source.
- The 6-month default, the `dateTo` inclusive-day rule, and the quotes-by-type query that filters only by date are all unchanged.
- The response shape and status codes are unchanged, as is the error log message.
- The SQL text is equivalent, but some indentation and line breaks inside the SQL strings changed. This has no effect on the query.

## Verification

- `node --check` passes on `route.js` and all five modules. Bun's transpiler also parses them.
- Every relative `@/lib/reports/*` import resolves to a file that exists.
- `@/app/api/utils/sql` and `@/app/api/utils/rbac` do not exist in this workspace. The original file imported them too, so this is not a regression. I left those imports unchanged.
- The dynamic import of `route.js` failed with `Cannot find package '@/app'`. This workspace has no `jsconfig`/`tsconfig` alias, so this is expected here and not caused by the refactor.
- No tests exist in the workspace, and I did not add any.

## Mistake to note

Partway through I created a placeholder `src/app/route.js.new` that was not part of the plan. I deleted it right away, and `src` now contains only the intended files.
